question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

Raghav, who studies tourism at present, is planning to go abroad after his graduation.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. is studying.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The phrase "at present" is a time marker that signals an action happening right now, which requires the present continuous tense (is/am/are + verb-ing). Hence "studies" must be replaced by "is studying".

◦ Example: She is working on the project at present.

• "Raghav" is a third person singular subject, so the correct auxiliary is "is" → "Raghav ... is studying tourism at present".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 ("will study") is future tense and contradicts "at present".

• Option 2 ("study") is a plural/base form and does not agree with the singular subject "Raghav".

• Option 3 ("studied") is past tense and again clashes with "at present".

NOTE

• Present continuous is used for (a) actions happening now, (b) temporary/ongoing actions, and (c) fixed future plans. Common time markers: now, at present, at the moment, currently, these days.

question:
Select the word that has the same meaning (SYNONYM) as the underlined word in the given sentence.

The disposal of hazardous waste in hospitals and factories is a serious problem and needs to be taken care of urgently.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. dangerous.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Hazardous" means risky or dangerous, i.e. likely to cause harm or damage. (खतरनाक)

◦ Example: Handling hazardous chemicals without gloves is unsafe.

• Its closest synonym among the options is "dangerous" — both describe something that poses a threat to safety or health.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 — Belligerent (युद्धप्रिय): aggressive or hostile / eager to fight.

• Option 3 — Hazy (धुंधला): unclear, misty or vague.

• Option 4 — Benign (सौम्य): gentle, kindly and harmless — the antonym of hazardous.

NOTE

• Other synonyms of hazardous frequently tested in SSC: perilous, precarious, unsafe, treacherous, risky.

question:
Select the present perfect tense of the verb given in the brackets to fill in the blank.

Alex _______ (study) two programming languages.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. has studied.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The present perfect tense is formed as: has/have + past participle (V3). The past participle of "study" is "studied".

• "Alex" is a third person singular subject, so it takes "has", giving "Alex has studied two programming languages".

◦ Example: He has finished his homework.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 ("have study") is doubly wrong — "have" is for plural subjects and "study" is not the past participle.

• Option 3 ("has been studying") is present perfect continuous, not present perfect.

• Option 4 ("had studied") is past perfect tense.

NOTE

• Present perfect (has/have + V3) links a past action to the present. Present perfect continuous (has/have been + V-ing) stresses the duration of an ongoing action.

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

The teacher checked / whether each of them / have a blanket / as it was a cold night.
option_2: as it was a cold night
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. have a blanket.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "each" is always singular and takes a singular verb. Therefore "each of them have" is wrong; it must be "each of them has".

◦ Correct: The teacher checked whether each of them has a blanket as it was a cold night.

• Words like each, every, either, neither, one of, everybody, everyone, anybody take a singular verb.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• "The teacher checked" — correct (simple past).

• "whether each of them" — correct usage of "whether" to introduce an indirect question.

• "as it was a cold night" — correct; "as" here means "because".

NOTE

• Remember: Each of + plural noun + singular verb → "Each of the students is present." Do not be misled by the plural noun after "of"; the verb agrees with "each".

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of 'scanty' in the sentence given below.

India has varied regions which have excess, moderate and deficient rainfall all through the year.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Deficient.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Scanty" means insufficient, meagre or too little in amount. (अल्प / अपर्याप्त)

◦ Example: The plants withered due to scanty rainfall.

• In the sentence, the word closest in meaning to scanty is "deficient", as both convey a shortage or inadequacy.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 — Excess: more than enough (antonym of scanty).

• Option 2 — Moderate: average / neither too much nor too little.

• Option 4 — Varied: of different kinds; diverse.

NOTE

• Synonyms of scanty: meagre, sparse, inadequate, insufficient, deficient. Antonyms: abundant, ample, plentiful, copious.

question:
Select the correctly spelt word to fill in the blank.

Arvind wanted to bake a cake for Riya's birthday, so he mixed the ____________, eggs and butter.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. flour.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Flour" is the correctly spelt word — a powder made by grinding wheat or other grains, used for baking. (आटा)

◦ Example: She used two cups of flour to make the bread.

• The context (baking a cake with "eggs and butter") requires the baking ingredient flour.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "flawer" and Option 4 "flover" are not real English words.

• Option 2 "flower" is a real word but means the blossom of a plant — a homophone of "flour" but wrong in this context.

NOTE

• Flour (baking powder from grain) and flower (bloom of a plant) are homophones — they sound alike but differ in spelling and meaning.

question:
Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word from the given sentence.

The gardener's meticulous care ensured the vibrent colours of the flowers.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Vibrent.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "Vibrent" is misspelt. The correct spelling is "vibrant", meaning bright, vivid and full of energy. (जीवंत / चटकीला)

◦ Example: The festival was full of vibrant colours and music.

• Spelling key: VIB + RANT (ends in "-ant", not "-ent").

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• "Gardener's" — correctly spelt (possessive form of gardener).

• "Care" — correctly spelt.

• "Meticulous" — correctly spelt; means showing great attention to detail.

NOTE

• Beware of the -ant / -ent confusion: correct spellings include vibrant, relevant, important, dominant (with "a"), and different, excellent, confident (with "e").

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

Please put the dishes in the __________ after you finish eating.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. sink.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A "sink" is a fixed basin in a kitchen with a water supply, where dishes are washed. It fits the context of clearing up after eating. (सिंक / बेसिन)

◦ Example: She left the dirty plates in the sink.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 — Shrink: to become smaller in size.

• Option 3 — Cinque: the number five (as on dice or cards) — irrelevant here.

• Option 4 — Sync: short for synchronise / to match in time — irrelevant here.

NOTE

• "Sink", "sync" and (loosely) "cinque" are near-homophones; only "sink" suits the kitchen context.

question: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. perepharal.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Perepharal" is misspelt. The correct spelling is "peripheral", meaning relating to the outer edge or of secondary importance. (परिधीय / गौण)

◦ Example: That issue is only peripheral to the main argument.

• Spelling key: PE + RI + PHE + RAL → "peri" (around) + "pheral".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• "Belated" — correctly spelt; means coming late (e.g., belated wishes).

• "Tentative" — correctly spelt; means not certain or fixed; provisional.

• "Stringent" — correctly spelt; means strict or severe (rules/standards).

NOTE

• Related words: periphery (noun) and peripheral (adjective). The root "peri-" (around) also appears in perimeter and periscope.

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.

Inspire
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Stimulate.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Inspire" means to encourage, motivate or stimulate someone to do or feel something. (प्रेरित करना)

◦ Example: Her speech inspired the whole team to work harder.

• "Stimulate" (to rouse to activity or interest) is the closest synonym.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 — Reach: to arrive at / extend to (unrelated in meaning).

• Option 3 — Aspire: to have a strong desire to achieve something — a near-confusable, but it means to aim, not to motivate others.

• Option 4 — Daunt: to discourage or intimidate — an antonym of inspire.

NOTE

• Synonyms of inspire: motivate, encourage, stimulate, energise, galvanise. Antonyms: discourage, dishearten, daunt, deter.

question:
Select the option that rectifies the spelling error in the given sentence.

The student received an A+ for her exellent performance.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. excellent.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The misspelt word in the sentence is "exellent". Its correct spelling is "excellent", meaning extremely good or outstanding. (उत्कृष्ट)

◦ Example: She gave an excellent presentation.

• Spelling key: EX + C + ELLENT — note the double "l" and the "xc" combination.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• "Performance" is already correctly spelt in the sentence, so options 1 ("perfarmance") and 3 ("performence") are wrong corrections.

• Option 4 "excelleant" is also a misspelling.

NOTE

• Related forms: excel (verb), excellence (noun), excellent (adjective), excellently (adverb).

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

The __________ of the scientific experiment raised questions about the validity of the results.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. ambiguity.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Ambiguity" means the quality of being open to more than one interpretation; vagueness or uncertainty. (अस्पष्टता / द्विअर्थता)

◦ Example: The ambiguity in the instructions confused the students.

• Only vagueness or uncertainty ("ambiguity") would logically "raise questions about the validity" of the results.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 — Transparency: openness and clarity — this would strengthen, not question, the results.

• Option 3 — Verbosity: use of too many words — does not, by itself, cast doubt on validity.

• Option 4 — Meticulousness: great attention to detail — this would support validity.

NOTE

• Synonyms of ambiguity: vagueness, obscurity, uncertainty, equivocation. Antonyms: clarity, transparency, lucidity.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

The student leader has ______ politics recently.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. entered.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The verb "entered" collocates naturally with "politics" — "to enter politics" means to begin taking part in political activity. (राजनीति में प्रवेश करना)

◦ Example: Many actors have entered politics after retiring from films.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 — "approached politics" is not a standard collocation and does not convey joining it.

• Option 3 — "gathered politics" is meaningless.

• Option 4 — "jumped politics" is incorrect; the idiom is "jumped into politics", which needs the preposition "into" (absent here).

NOTE

• Useful collocations: enter politics, join politics, quit politics, dominate politics. With the preposition, "jump into politics" is acceptable, but "jump politics" is not.

question:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don't find any error, mark 'No error' as your answer.

I am / cleaning the sofa / when she called me.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. I am.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The clause "when she called me" is in the past tense, so the main clause must also be in the past continuous, not the present. Therefore "I am" should be "I was".

◦ Correct: I was cleaning the sofa when she called me.

• The structure "was/were + V-ing ... when + simple past" describes a longer past action interrupted by a shorter one.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• "cleaning the sofa" — correct (the -ing form after the auxiliary).

• "when she called me" — correct (simple past for the interrupting action).

NOTE

• Rule of sequence of tenses: when the subordinate clause is in the past, the main clause is generally in a past form. Past continuous (was/were + V-ing) sets the background action.

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

The society / of the / our place / is good.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. of the.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A possessive determiner ("our") cannot follow the article "the". The article "the" is redundant here and must be removed. The correct phrase is "the society of our place".

◦ Correct: The society of our place is good.

• We do not use two determiners ("the" + "our") together before a noun.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• "The society" — correct.

• "our place" — correct.

• "is good" — correct (singular verb for the singular subject "society").

NOTE

• Articles (a, an, the) and possessives (my, our, his, its) are both determiners; only one may precede a noun. "the our place" → "our place"; "a my friend" → "a friend of mine".

question:
Select the most appropriate expression that can substitute the underlined word in the given sentence.

Sonali is contemplating whether to accept the offer from Saanvi or not; she is still not in a position to be able to arrive at a decision.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. chewing the cud.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "to chew the cud" means to think deeply and at length; to ponder or reflect before deciding. (गहराई से सोच-विचार करना)

◦ Example: He sat quietly, chewing the cud over the job offer.

• This matches "contemplating ... still not ... able to arrive at a decision".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 — Raising the eyebrows: to show surprise or disapproval.

• Option 2 — Blowing hot and cold: to keep changing one's opinion / be inconsistent — close, but it stresses vacillation, not deep reflection.

• Option 3 — Getting her act together: to become organised and start performing effectively.

NOTE

• "Chew the cud" comes from cattle re-chewing partly digested food; figuratively it means to mull something over. Synonymous idioms: to mull over, to turn something over in one's mind.

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the sentence.

She was deeply effected by the news, to the point of tears.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. affected by.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Affect" is a verb meaning to influence or move emotionally, whereas "effect" is usually a noun meaning result. The sentence needs the verb, so "effected" is wrong.

• In the passive voice, the correct structure is "affected by" — "She was deeply affected by the news."

◦ Example: The whole town was affected by the flood.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 — "affect from" is grammatically wrong (wrong preposition and active form).

• Option 2 — "effected from" wrongly uses "effect" as the verb.

• Option 3 — "affected of" uses the wrong preposition ("of" instead of "by").

NOTE

• Affect = to influence (verb); Effect = result (noun) — "The medicine affected her, and the effect lasted a day." Rarely, "effect" is a verb meaning "to bring about" (to effect a change).

question: You overhear someone say, "He's always on cloud nine." What does this idiom mean in the given context?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Extremely happy.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "on cloud nine" means extremely happy, elated or delighted. (अत्यधिक प्रसन्न)

◦ Example: She was on cloud nine when she cleared the SSC exam.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Often absent", Option 3 "Frequently daydreaming" and Option 4 "Always busy" do not capture the sense of great joy conveyed by the idiom.

• "Frequently daydreaming" is a common trap because clouds suggest the sky, but the idiom is strictly about happiness.

NOTE

• Related "happiness" idioms often tested in SSC: over the moon, on top of the world, walking on air, in seventh heaven, tickled pink.

question:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don't find any error, mark 'No error' as your answer.

She is / as more intelligent as / her brothers are.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. as more intelligent as.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The comparison structure "as ... as" takes the positive degree of the adjective, not the comparative. So "as more intelligent as" is wrong; it must be "as intelligent as".

◦ Correct: She is as intelligent as her brothers are.

• We cannot mix the comparative ("more intelligent") with the "as ... as" construction.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• "She is" — correct.

• "her brothers are" — correct.

NOTE

• Degrees of comparison: positive with "as ... as" (as tall as); comparative with "than" (taller than / more intelligent than); superlative with "the" (the tallest). Never combine "more" with "as ... as".

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

He dropped out / at his friend's house / on his way home / the day before yesterday.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. He dropped out.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The phrasal verb "drop out" means to leave or withdraw (e.g., from school/college), which does not fit the context of stopping by a friend's house on the way home. The intended verb is "dropped in / dropped by" (to make a short casual visit).

◦ Correct: He dropped in at his friend's house on his way home the day before yesterday.

• "Drop in/by" = to visit briefly; "drop out" = to quit.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• "at his friend's house" — correct.

• "on his way home" — correct.

• "the day before yesterday" — correct time expression.

NOTE

• Phrasal verbs with "drop": drop in/by (visit briefly), drop out (quit), drop off (leave someone/something; fall asleep), drop off (decline).

question:
Read the following passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

It was one January morning, very early — a pinching, frosty morning — the cove all grey ____1____ hoar-frost and the ripple lapping softly on the stones. The captain had ____2____ earlier than usual and set out down the beach. Mother was upstairs with father and I was ____3____ the breakfast table against the captain's return when the parlour door opened and a man stepped in on whom I had never set my eyes before. He was a pale, tallowy creature, wanting two fingers of the left hand, and ____4____ he wore a cutlass, he did not look much like a fighter. I had always my eye open for seafaring ____5____ with one leg or two, and I remember this one puzzled me.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. with.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The phrase "the cove all grey with hoar-frost" uses "with" to show the cause / covering — the cove looked grey because it was covered with frost. (के कारण / से ढका हुआ)

◦ Example: The fields were white with snow.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Options 2 and 3 — "among / amongst" indicate being in the middle of a group of things and do not fit a covering of frost.

• Option 4 — "about" (around/concerning) does not suit the sense of being coated with frost.

NOTE

• The passage is the opening of "Treasure Island" by Robert Louis Stevenson. "With" is commonly used to describe a covering: covered with, filled with, grey with frost, red with anger.

question:
Read the following passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

It was one January morning, very early — a pinching, frosty morning — the cove all grey ____1____ hoar-frost and the ripple lapping softly on the stones. The captain had ____2____ earlier than usual and set out down the beach. Mother was upstairs with father and I was ____3____ the breakfast table against the captain's return when the parlour door opened and a man stepped in on whom I had never set my eyes before. He was a pale, tallowy creature, wanting two fingers of the left hand, and ____4____ he wore a cutlass, he did not look much like a fighter. I had always my eye open for seafaring ____5____ with one leg or two, and I remember this one puzzled me.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. risen.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence "The captain had risen earlier than usual and set out down the beach" requires the past participle of "rise" (rise – rose – risen), meaning got out of bed / woke up. (उठ जाना)

◦ Example: He had risen at dawn to catch the train.

• The present perfect / past perfect structure "had + V3" needs the participle "risen".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Options 1 and 4 — "danced / waltzed" make no sense with "earlier than usual and set out down the beach".

• Option 3 — "written" is unrelated to getting up early.

NOTE

• "Rise" (rise–rose–risen) is intransitive and takes no object: the sun rises. "Raise" (raise–raised–raised) is transitive and takes an object: raise your hand.

question:
Read the following passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

It was one January morning, very early — a pinching, frosty morning — the cove all grey ____1____ hoar-frost and the ripple lapping softly on the stones. The captain had ____2____ earlier than usual and set out down the beach. Mother was upstairs with father and I was ____3____ the breakfast table against the captain's return when the parlour door opened and a man stepped in on whom I had never set my eyes before. He was a pale, tallowy creature, wanting two fingers of the left hand, and ____4____ he wore a cutlass, he did not look much like a fighter. I had always my eye open for seafaring ____5____ with one leg or two, and I remember this one puzzled me.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. laying.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "I was laying the breakfast table" means setting / arranging the table with plates, cutlery, etc. "Lay the table" is a fixed expression. (मेज़ लगाना)

◦ Example: Please lay the table; dinner is almost ready.

• "Lay" (lay – laid – laid) is transitive and takes an object ("the breakfast table"); hence "laying" is correct here.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 — "lying" is from "lie" (to recline / to tell an untruth) and is intransitive; it cannot take the object "table".

• Options 3 and 4 — "throwing / playing" the breakfast table are illogical.

NOTE

• Lay (transitive, needs object): lay–laid–laid → "lay the table". Lie (intransitive, no object): lie–lay–lain → "lie down on the bed". This lay/lie distinction is a frequent SSC trap.

question:
Read the following passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

It was one January morning, very early — a pinching, frosty morning — the cove all grey ____1____ hoar-frost and the ripple lapping softly on the stones. The captain had ____2____ earlier than usual and set out down the beach. Mother was upstairs with father and I was ____3____ the breakfast table against the captain's return when the parlour door opened and a man stepped in on whom I had never set my eyes before. He was a pale, tallowy creature, wanting two fingers of the left hand, and ____4____ he wore a cutlass, he did not look much like a fighter. I had always my eye open for seafaring ____5____ with one leg or two, and I remember this one puzzled me.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. though.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Though" is a conjunction meaning although / in spite of the fact that. It fits the contrast: "though he wore a cutlass, he did not look much like a fighter." (यद्यपि / हालाँकि)

◦ Example: Though it was raining, they continued the match.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 — "through" (a preposition meaning across/by means of) does not join the two contrasting clauses.

• Option 2 — "throw" (to hurl) is a verb and unrelated.

• Option 4 — "threw" is the past tense of "throw" and unrelated.

NOTE

• Do not confuse the homophones: though (although), through (across / by means of), thorough (complete/detailed), thought (past of think), threw (past of throw).

question:
Read the following passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

It was one January morning, very early — a pinching, frosty morning — the cove all grey ____1____ hoar-frost and the ripple lapping softly on the stones. The captain had ____2____ earlier than usual and set out down the beach. Mother was upstairs with father and I was ____3____ the breakfast table against the captain's return when the parlour door opened and a man stepped in on whom I had never set my eyes before. He was a pale, tallowy creature, wanting two fingers of the left hand, and ____4____ he wore a cutlass, he did not look much like a fighter. I had always my eye open for seafaring ____5____ with one leg or two, and I remember this one puzzled me.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. men.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The phrase "seafaring men with one leg or two" refers to sailors / people who work at sea. "Seafaring" describes people (men), and the following clause "with one leg or two" clearly points to human beings. (नाविक / समुद्री यात्री)

◦ Example: The port was full of hardy seafaring men.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Options 1 and 4 — "plants / flowers" cannot be "seafaring" nor have "one leg or two".

• Option 2 — "birds" does not collocate with "seafaring" in this narrative about sailors.

NOTE

• In "Treasure Island", the narrator (young Jim Hawkins) watches for a one-legged sailor, so "men" fits both grammar and story context.

question: A party recognised by the Election Commission of India that secures at least __________ of the total votes in the General Election to Lok Sabha or Legislative Assembly in four or more states in addition to winning four Lok Sabha seats is called a National Party.
solution_text:
The correct answer is six per cent.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• As per the conditions laid down by the Election Commission of India (ECI), one way for a party to be recognised as a National Party is to secure at least 6% of the total valid votes in a general election to the Lok Sabha or a State Legislative Assembly in four or more States, and win at least 4 seats in the Lok Sabha. (राष्ट्रीय दल)

• A party can also become a National Party by (a) winning 2% of Lok Sabha seats from at least 3 different States, or (b) being recognised as a State party in at least 4 States.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Recognition of political parties is governed by the Election Symbols (Reservation and Allotment) Order, 1968.

• Benefits of national recognition include a reserved election symbol, free time on Doordarshan/All India Radio, and land for a party office.

NOTE

• Do not confuse this with the criteria for a State Party, which requires 6% of votes plus 2 seats in an Assembly election, or 3% of Assembly seats, among other conditions.

question: Which musical duo is part of the Khayal singing lineage of the Banaras Gharana?
option_2: Salamat Ali and Nazakat Ali Khan
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rajan and Sajan Mishra.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Pandit Rajan Mishra and Pandit Sajan Mishra were a celebrated Khayal-singing duo of the Banaras (Benares) Gharana of Hindustani classical music. (बनारस घराना — ख़याल गायन)

• They were awarded the Padma Bhushan (2007) and the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award for their contribution to classical vocal music.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Khayal is the dominant genre of modern Hindustani classical vocal music, valued for its improvisation; the word means "imagination".

• The Banaras Gharana is one of the major gharanas, especially renowned for thumri and tabla as well.

NOTE

• Salamat Ali & Nazakat Ali Khan belonged to the Sham Chaurasi Gharana; the other pairs are not associated with the Banaras Khayal lineage.

question: The IUPAC name of CH₃-(CH₂)₁₈-CH₃ is __________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is icosane.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The formula CH₃–(CH₂)₁₈–CH₃ has 2 + 18 = 20 carbon atoms in a straight chain. The straight-chain alkane with 20 carbons is icosane (also spelt eicosane), formula C₂₀H₄₂. (आइकोसेन — C₂₀)

• The general formula of an alkane is CₙH₂ₙ₊₂; for n = 20, that gives C₂₀H₄₂.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• IUPAC names by carbon count: Decane (C₁₀), Undecane (C₁₁), Dodecane (C₁₂), Icosane (C₂₀), Triacontane (C₃₀).

• "Icosa-" is the Greek prefix for twenty (as in icosahedron, a 20-faced solid).

NOTE

• Option 2 Decane = C₁₀, Option 4 Dodecane = C₁₂, and Option 1 Triacontane = C₃₀ — none has 20 carbons, so only icosane fits.

question: Which of the following can be a basis of difference between a salamander and a house-wall lizard apart from their habitat?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Scales on the skin.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A salamander is an amphibian with moist, smooth, scaleless skin, whereas a house-wall lizard (a gecko) is a reptile whose body is covered with dry scales. Thus, the presence or absence of scales on the skin distinguishes them. (शल्क / स्केल)

• Reptiles have scaly, waterproof skin; amphibians have thin, moist skin used partly for respiration.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Both are cold-blooded (ectothermic), so "cold-blood" cannot differentiate them (Option 2 wrong).

• Both generally lay eggs, so egg-laying is not a distinguishing feature (Option 1 wrong).

• Both amphibians and most reptiles (except crocodiles) have a three-chambered heart, so that too is not distinguishing (Option 4 wrong).

NOTE

• Salamander → Class Amphibia; House lizard/gecko → Class Reptilia. Amphibians typically need water/moist surroundings to breed and keep their skin moist.

question: Which of the following novels is NOT written by Aravind Adiga?
solution_text:
The correct answer is The English Teacher.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "The English Teacher" (1945) was written by R. K. Narayan, not by Aravind Adiga. It is a semi-autobiographical novel set in Narayan's fictional town of Malgudi. (आर. के. नारायण)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Aravind Adiga is an Indian-Australian writer who won the Man Booker Prize in 2008 for his debut novel "The White Tiger".

• Other novels by Adiga include "Last Man in Tower" (2011), "Selection Day" (2016) and the story collection "Between the Assassinations".

NOTE

• R. K. Narayan's famous works include Swami and Friends, The Guide, The Bachelor of Arts, The Man-Eater of Malgudi and Malgudi Days.

question: In which stadium did Indian cricketer Saurav Ganguly take off and waive his t-shirt?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Lord's Stadium, England.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The former Indian captain Sourav Ganguly famously took off his shirt and waved it from the balcony of Lord's Cricket Ground, London, after India won the NatWest Series final against England in 2002. (लॉर्ड्स, इंग्लैंड — 2002 नैटवेस्ट फाइनल)

• The gesture was a reply to Andrew Flintoff, who had earlier removed his shirt in Mumbai.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Lord's in London is often called the "Home of Cricket" and is owned by the Marylebone Cricket Club (MCC).

• In that 2002 final, India chased down a large total, with Yuvraj Singh and Mohammad Kaif playing a match-winning partnership.

NOTE

• Sourav Ganguly is nicknamed the "Prince of Kolkata" / "Dada" and later served as President of the BCCI (2019–2022).

question: The PM-SVANidhi Scheme (2020) is run by which Ministry of the Government of India?
option_3: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• PM SVANidhi (PM Street Vendor's AtmaNirbhar Nidhi), launched in June 2020, is administered by the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA). (आवासन एवं शहरी कार्य मंत्रालय)

• It is a micro-credit scheme that provides collateral-free working capital loans to urban street vendors to help them resume livelihoods affected by the COVID-19 pandemic.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The scheme offers an initial loan of ₹10,000, enhanced to ₹20,000 and then ₹50,000 on timely repayment, along with an interest subsidy of 7% and incentives for digital transactions.

NOTE

• "SVANidhi" combines "Svavlamban" (self-reliance) with "Nidhi" (fund). It supports the Atmanirbhar Bharat vision.

question: After which of the following Acts did India come to be governed in the name of the British crown?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Government of India Act, 1858.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Government of India Act, 1858, passed after the Revolt of 1857, ended the rule of the East India Company and transferred the governance of India directly to the British Crown. (1858 का भारत सरकार अधिनियम)

• It created the office of the Secretary of State for India, assisted by a 15-member Council of India, and changed the title of the Governor-General to Viceroy (Lord Canning being the first Viceroy).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The Act is also known as the "Act for the Good Government of India".

• It followed Queen Victoria's Proclamation (1858), which promised religious tolerance and equal treatment of Indians.

NOTE

• Charter Act 1833 made the Governor-General of Bengal the Governor-General of India (Lord William Bentinck); Charter Act 1853 introduced open competition for the civil services.

question: Hornbill festival is organised every year in which of the following states?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Nagaland.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Hornbill Festival is celebrated every year from 1 to 10 December in Nagaland, at the Naga Heritage Village, Kisama, near Kohima. (हॉर्नबिल महोत्सव — नागालैंड)

• Called the "Festival of Festivals", it showcases the culture, dances, music, crafts and food of all major Naga tribes. It is named after the hornbill bird, revered in Naga folklore.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Nagaland was formed as a state on 1 December 1963; its capital is Kohima.

• Other festivals of Nagaland include Moatsu and Sekrenyi.

NOTE

• Do not confuse it with festivals of other NE states — e.g., Bihu (Assam), Losar (Ladakh/Sikkim), Wangala (Meghalaya).

question: At the Sansad Ratna Awards 2023, who among the following received the Dr. APJ Abdul Kalam Lifetime Achievement Award?
solution_text:
The correct answer is TK Rangarajan.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• At the Sansad Ratna Awards 2023, former Rajya Sabha member TK Rangarajan (CPI-M, Tamil Nadu) was honoured with the Dr. APJ Abdul Kalam Lifetime Achievement Award for his parliamentary contribution. (संसद रत्न पुरस्कार 2023)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The Sansad Ratna Awards honour top-performing Members of Parliament based on parameters such as debates, private member bills and questions raised, using data from PRS Legislative Research.

• The awards were instituted in 2010, inspired by a suggestion of Dr. A. P. J. Abdul Kalam.

NOTE

• Former PM HD Deve Gowda also received a lifetime achievement recognition at the Sansad Ratna Awards in an earlier year, which is why he is a common distractor.

question: When was National Judicial Commission Bill, which is a private member bill to regulate the appointment of judges through the National Judicial Commission, introduced in Rajya Sabha?
solution_text:
The correct answer is December 2022.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The National Judicial Commission Bill, 2022 — a private member's bill seeking to regulate the appointment of judges through a National Judicial Commission — was introduced in the Rajya Sabha in December 2022. (राष्ट्रीय न्यायिक आयोग विधेयक)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• A private member's bill is one introduced by an MP who is not a Minister; such bills are taken up on Fridays and rarely become law.

• Judicial appointments in India are currently made through the Collegium System, evolved from the Second and Third Judges Cases.

NOTE

• The earlier National Judicial Appointments Commission (NJAC) Act, 2014 (99th Constitutional Amendment) was struck down as unconstitutional by the Supreme Court in 2015, restoring the Collegium.

question: The Mughal emperor, Babur was a devotee of the ______ Sufi Silsila.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Naqshbandi.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The first Mughal emperor, Babur, was a follower/devotee of the Naqshbandi Sufi Silsila (order). This order had considerable influence in Central Asia, from where the Mughals came. (नक्शबंदी सिलसिला)

• The Naqshbandi order in India was later strengthened by Khwaja Baqi Billah and Sheikh Ahmad Sirhindi (Mujaddid Alf-i-Sani).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Major Sufi silsilas in India: Chishti (Khwaja Moinuddin Chishti of Ajmer), Suhrawardi, Qadiri and Naqshbandi.

• The Chishti order was the most popular and preached love, tolerance and simple living.

NOTE

• Sufism stresses a personal, mystical union with God; a "silsila" is a spiritual chain/order tracing back to a founding saint.

question: Which of the following dances of Goa is performed to celebrate the victory of the Maratha warriors over the Portuguese?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ghodemodni.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Ghode Modni" is a martial folk dance of Goa performed by dancers dressed as warriors on dummy horses, commemorating the victory of the Maratha warriors over the Portuguese. (घोडेमोडनी — गोवा)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Other folk dances of Goa include Dekhni, Fugdi, Dhalo, Kunbi, Corridinho (Portuguese-influenced) and Goff (a dance involving weaving of coloured cords).

NOTE

• "Ghode" means horse; the dance is usually performed during festivals and processions in the Bicholim and Sattari regions of Goa.

question: Which of the following Kathak dancers received the Padma Shri of 2022?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kamalini and Nalini Asthana.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Kathak exponents Kamalini Asthana and Nalini Asthana (the "Asthana sisters") were jointly awarded the Padma Shri in 2022 for their contribution to art (dance). (कथक — पद्म श्री 2022)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Kathak is one of the eight classical dance forms of India, associated mainly with North India and known for fast footwork (tatkar), spins (chakkars) and expressive storytelling (abhinaya).

• Shovana Narayan (Option 3) is another eminent Kathak dancer and a Padma Shri awardee, but of an earlier year, making her a common distractor.

NOTE

• The eight classical dances: Bharatanatyam (TN), Kathak (North India), Kathakali & Mohiniyattam (Kerala), Kuchipudi (AP), Odissi (Odisha), Manipuri (Manipur), Sattriya (Assam).

question: The Bidar Fort of Karnataka is irregularly ______ in shape.
solution_text:
The correct answer is rhomboid.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Bidar Fort in Karnataka is irregularly rhomboid (rhombus-like) in shape. (बीदर किला — विषम समचतुर्भुज आकार)

• It was rebuilt by Ahmad Shah Wali Bahmani in 1427 when he shifted the Bahmani capital from Gulbarga to Bidar.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The fort is famous for its triple moat (partly rock-cut), its many gates such as the Sherza Darwaza, and monuments like the Rangin Mahal, Solah Khamba Mosque and Takht Mahal.

• Bidar is also known for Bidriware, a metal handicraft with silver inlay.

NOTE

• A rhomboid is a parallelogram whose adjacent sides are unequal — the fort's outline resembles this irregular four-sided shape.

question:
A coastal area was flooded with sea water and resulted in heavy salt deposits in the nearby area. After a few days, it was observed that many plants died. Based on these statements, which of the following is the most probable cause of the plant deaths?

A. Plants died due to infection from sea water borne germs.  B. Plants died due to absence of sunlight.  C. Plants died due to plasmolysis in the plant cells.  D. Plants died because they were eaten by sea organisms.
solution_text:
The correct answer is C — Plants died due to plasmolysis in the plant cells (marked as Option 2).

IMPORTANT POINTS

• When soil is flooded with salty sea water, the surrounding solution becomes hypertonic (higher solute concentration than the cell sap). Water then moves out of the plant cells by osmosis, the protoplasm shrinks away from the cell wall, and the cell undergoes plasmolysis, leading to the death of the plants. (जीवद्रव्यकुंचन / प्लास्मोलिसिस)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2 (statement C).

Additional Information

• Osmosis is the movement of solvent (water) from a region of lower solute concentration to higher solute concentration across a semipermeable membrane.

• In a hypotonic solution a cell gains water and becomes turgid; in a hypertonic solution it loses water and becomes plasmolysed.

NOTE

• The salt causes water loss, not germs (A), lack of sunlight (B) or sea organisms (D) — hence plasmolysis is the correct scientific reason.

question: According to Indian Meteorology, which of the following is NOT a season experienced in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Equatorial season.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The India Meteorological Department (IMD) recognises four seasons, and "Equatorial season" is NOT one of them. (भूमध्यरेखीय ऋतु — भारत में नहीं)

• The four seasons as per IMD are:

◦ The cold weather season / winter (December–February)

◦ The hot weather season / summer (March–May)

◦ The southwest monsoon / rainy season (June–September)

◦ The retreating monsoon / post-monsoon season (October–November)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• India has a monsoon type of climate, dominated by the seasonal reversal of winds — the southwest monsoon brings most of the annual rainfall.

NOTE

• An "equatorial" climate (hot and wet all year) is characteristic of regions near the Equator like the Amazon and Congo basins, not of India.

question: Bawris are traditionally used for:
solution_text:
The correct answer is storing and recharging water.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Bawris (baolis / stepwells) are traditional water-harvesting structures, typically deep wells with steps leading down to the water level, used for storing water and recharging groundwater, especially in the arid regions of Rajasthan and Gujarat. (बावड़ी — जल संचयन)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Famous stepwells include the Chand Baori (Abhaneri, Rajasthan) and the Rani ki Vav (Patan, Gujarat), a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

• Such structures also served as cool resting places and community gathering spots.

NOTE

• Other traditional water-harvesting systems: Kund/Tanka (Rajasthan), Johad (check dams), Ahar-Pyne (Bihar), Zabo (Nagaland), Kuhls (Himachal).

question: Who was the Indian match referee in the ICC - T20 World Cup 2021 tournament?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Javagal Srinath.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Former Indian fast bowler Javagal Srinath served as an ICC match referee in the ICC Men's T20 World Cup 2021, held in the UAE and Oman. (जवागल श्रीनाथ — मैच रेफरी)

• He is a member of the Emirates ICC Elite Panel of Match Referees.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The 2021 T20 World Cup was won by Australia, who beat New Zealand in the final; it was Australia's first men's T20 World Cup title.

• A match referee enforces the ICC Code of Conduct, imposes penalties for breaches and oversees the spirit of the game.

NOTE

• Javagal Srinath is one of India's finest pace bowlers and the only Indian fast bowler to take 300+ ODI wickets.

question: The Universal Adult Franchise in Indian Constitution is applicable to Indian Citizens from the age of ______________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 18 years.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Under Universal Adult Franchise, every citizen of India who is 18 years of age or above has the right to vote, without discrimination of caste, religion, sex, etc. (सार्वभौमिक वयस्क मताधिकार — 18 वर्ष)

• The voting age was reduced from 21 to 18 years by the 61st Constitutional Amendment Act, 1988, which came into effect in 1989.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Universal Adult Franchise is guaranteed under Article 326 of the Constitution.

• It reflects the democratic principle of "one person, one vote, one value".

NOTE

• Minimum age qualifications: voter – 18; MLA/MP (Lok Sabha) – 25; Rajya Sabha member – 30; President/Vice-President – 35.

question: Who among the following deciphered the Brahmi Script of the Mauryan period?
solution_text:
The correct answer is James Prinsep.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• James Prinsep, an officer of the East India Company and secretary of the Asiatic Society, deciphered the Brahmi (and Kharosthi) scripts in 1837. This unlocked the reading of Ashoka's edicts and revealed the identity of "Devanampiya Piyadasi" as Emperor Ashoka. (ब्राह्मी लिपि — जेम्स प्रिंसेप, 1837)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Brahmi is the ancestor of most modern Indian scripts and was written left to right.

• The decipherment opened up the systematic study of ancient Indian epigraphy and history.

NOTE

• James Mill wrote "The History of British India"; Rakhal Das Banerji discovered Mohenjo-daro; H. H. Risley conducted early census and ethnographic surveys of India.

question: In general, deficit is considered as a ________ concept.
solution_text:
The correct answer is flow.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A deficit (such as a fiscal or budget deficit) is measured over a period of time (e.g., a financial year), so it is a flow concept, not a stock. (प्रवाह / फ्लो अवधारणा)

• A flow variable is measured per unit of time (e.g., income, expenditure, deficit), whereas a stock variable is measured at a point of time (e.g., wealth, capital, debt).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Examples of flow: national income, investment, deficit, exports. Examples of stock: money supply, national debt, foreign exchange reserves.

• Accumulated deficits over years add up to public debt, which is a stock.

NOTE

• Remember: a deficit is a flow, but the debt it creates is a stock — a favourite economics distinction in SSC exams.

question: Who was appointed as the Viceroy of India in place of Lord Wavell in February 1947?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Lord Mountbatten.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Lord Louis Mountbatten was appointed Viceroy of India in February 1947, replacing Lord Wavell. He was the last Viceroy of British India. (लॉर्ड माउंटबेटन — अंतिम वायसराय)

• He presented the Mountbatten Plan (3 June 1947), which led to the partition of India and the passing of the Indian Independence Act, 1947.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• After independence, Mountbatten became the first Governor-General of independent India (1947–48); C. Rajagopalachari succeeded him as the first Indian Governor-General.

NOTE

• Sequence of related Viceroys: Linlithgow (1936–43) → Wavell (1943–47) → Mountbatten (1947). Lord Irwin (Halifax) was associated with the Gandhi–Irwin Pact (1931).

question: Which of the following age groups is considered as working population or working age in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 15-59 years.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In India, the working-age population (economically active age group) is generally taken as 15–59 years. People in this band are considered capable of productive work. (कार्यशील जनसंख्या — 15–59 वर्ष)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The population is broadly divided into: children (0–14 years), working-age adults (15–59 years) and the aged (60 years and above).

• The dependency ratio compares the dependent population (children + aged) to the working-age population.

NOTE

• India is currently benefiting from a demographic dividend — a large share of its population is in the working-age group of 15–59 years.

question: What is the approx width of broad-gauge railway network in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1.6 metres.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The broad gauge in India has a track width (distance between the two rails) of 1,676 mm ≈ 1.676 metres, which is approximately 1.6 metres. (ब्रॉड गेज — लगभग 1.6 मीटर)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Indian railway gauges: Broad Gauge – 1.676 m, Metre Gauge – 1.000 m, Narrow Gauge – 0.762 m / 0.610 m.

• Under "Project Unigauge", Indian Railways has been converting most routes to broad gauge for uniformity and efficiency.

NOTE

• Indian Railways is one of the largest rail networks in the world under a single management and is a major mode of freight and passenger transport.
